narrative.overview: This is Payload's own admin, left almost entirely alone. There is no injected brand accent anywhere in the shell — no primary blue, no logo color bleeding into buttons or focus rings. Every panel, table, and form runs on Payload's native grayscale elevation scale and its three semantic status colors, because the actual users (HR admins, HACCP officers, CRM approvers, and — during a shift — waiter, kitchen, and cashier staff) are scanning dense operational data under time pressure, not evaluating a brand. Volume is earned, not default. The one deliberate exception is the FnB order boards: real-time, floor-paced screens where a waiter, chef, or cashier needs to read table/status/action from across a kitchen pass or a service line. There, and only there, the system goes loud — thick black borders and hard offset shadows in a contained neubrutalist register — while still built entirely from Payload's own tokens, so it never breaks dark mode. A second, separate register lives behind the same shell: the guest-facing public surfaces this admin drives (public Forms, FnB menu/ordering pages, and Site Pages). Those are intentionally white-label — each is skinned per operator via daisyUI's data-theme mechanism, not by this admin's own quiet palette. The admin stays quiet so the operator's brand can be loud where guests actually see it.
keyCharacteristics: No brand accent in the admin shell — grayscale elevation + status colors only, straight from Payload's defaults.
Flat at rest; shadows are ambient and reserved for floating surfaces.
One contained neubrutalist exception (FnB order boards) — bold, but scoped, and never a template for other urgent surfaces.
Guest-facing surfaces (Forms, FnB pages, Site Pages) run a separate, per-operator white-label theme system layered on daisyUI.
Trilingual guest content (English / Arabic / French); Tajawal exists specifically for Arabic.

rules.name: The No-Accent Rule
rules.body: The admin shell has no primary brand color. If a new admin surface seems to need one, that's a signal to lean on Status Blue (Payload's own accent) or stay neutral — not to introduce a new hex value.

rules.name: The Operator-Owns-The-Palette Rule
rules.body: A guest page's color is never hardcoded in a component — it's selected via the theme field (or a fully custom pasted daisyUI theme for a new brand). Redesigning a guest surface means adding or editing a theme block, not touching component code.

rules.name: The Locale-Aware Type Rule
rules.body: The platform serves English, Arabic, and French guest content. Tajawal is the font offered specifically for Arabic; don't assume a Latin-only font pairing will hold up once a page's locale switches.

rules.name: The FnB-Only Rule
rules.body: The neubrutalist hard-offset shadow and its thick ink-colored border are confirmed as scoped to the FnB order boards specifically. Do not extend this treatment to any other admin surface unless explicitly instructed.

rules.name: The daisyUI-First Rule
rules.body: Every guest theme is a genuine daisyUI theme object, so components should be built from daisyUI's own primitives (btn, card, modal, badge, input, navbar, menu, alert) so they inherit primary/secondary/base-* automatically from whichever data-theme the page is in. Public Forms already does this correctly; the FnB ordering flow (cart bar, table picker) is a known deviation and a fix target.

rules.name: The Verified-Font-Gap Rule
rules.body: Doha Oasis's official headers use Noah + Baskerville (accent words) with Poppins Extra Light body text and Frutiger LT + Geeza Pro for Arabic headers / Tajawal for Arabic body. Doha Quest's official headers use Playfair Display Bold with Futura body text and Tajawal for Arabic. Baskerville, Frutiger LT, Geeza Pro, Playfair Display, and Futura are all missing from the current uploadable font list (Poppins, Tajawal, Urbanist, Gilroy, Noah) -- adding them is a legitimate accuracy fix, not scope creep.

dos: Do reference Payload's --theme-elevation-* / --theme-success/warning/error-* custom properties for any new admin UI, never a hardcoded hex or a Tailwind gray/green/red utility.
Do use Payload's native Button and Pill components for standard admin actions and status display before reaching for a hand-rolled equivalent.
Do keep new admin surfaces in the quiet register (1px hairline borders, rounded/rounded-md corners, ambient shadows only on floating elements) even when the surface itself is time-critical.
Do theme new or edited guest-facing pages through the existing theme field / operator theme blocks, using operator-based names for any new palette.
Do account for Arabic (and French) when touching guest-facing typography or layout.

Do build guest-facing UI from daisyUI's own component classes (btn, card, modal, badge, input, navbar, menu, alert) first, the way public Forms already does — they inherit the active data-theme automatically.
Do treat each operator's official brand book as the source of truth over what's currently coded when a guest surface is being brought to full accuracy.
donts: Don't reuse the FnB order board's neubrutalist hard-offset shadow or thick ink border on any other admin surface unless explicitly instructed.
Don't introduce a primary brand accent into the admin shell.
Don't hardcode Tailwind palette colors (bg-green-600, bg-red-600, etc.) for status/action UI where a Payload theme token already exists.
Don't hardcode a guest-facing color, font, or radius into a shared component — every guest page's look is theme-driven and operator-owned.

Don't hand-roll a guest-facing button, card, or modal with one-off Tailwind + CSS-var recipes when daisyUI already ships the primitive — the FnB cart bar and table picker currently do this and are a fix target.

Don't reuse the banyan-tree-lululemon theme's black/white palette for a general Banyan Tree Doha page — it was built for a one-time, now-retired collab form and is correct as-is; a plain Banyan Tree Doha page should use the operator's actual accent, #85754E.
